item.title: Scotland men slip up at European curling before semi-finals live on BBC
item.description: Scotland's women are next up against Lithuania on Friday afternoon [Getty Images] Scotland's men will face unbeaten Sweden in the European Curling Championships semi-finals after losing their 100% record in the round-robin following a disappointing 6-5 defeat by Italy. It means that Grant Hardie's rink finish second in Group A behind Stefano Spiller's side, who face the Czech Republic in the other semi-final. World and Olympic champion Oskar Eriksson's Swedes beat Poland 7-2 to secure top place in Group B with a 100% record, while Lukas Klima's Czechs qualified as runners-up despite losing their second match of the round robin - 8-4 to Sergio Vez's Spain. Against Italy, the Scots were always playing catch-up after losing two at the opening end. Hardie's rink did manage to edge ahead at 4-3 after the sixth end, but Italy took two at the seventh and, although the Scots then levelled to take the match into an extra-end, lead Ross Whyte was short with his final stone to concede defeat. Before the men's semi-finals, Scotland's women are also in last-four action against Switzerland (12:30 GMT), with both matches live on the BBC iPlayer and online. Fay Henderson's rink clinched a place in the last four with a game to spare after a tense extra-end triumph over Estonia on Thursday. Having suffered their first defeat of the group stage earlier, losing 10-2 to Sweden, they hit back from 8-3 down to score three and then steal two to force an extra end. Then Scotland managed a crucial steal to win it 9-8 when Estonia skip Marie Kaldvee was unable to clear a Scottish stone with a raise-takeout. Fay Henderson's rink ended off their Group B campaign with a 7-5 victory over Lithuania as they qualified as runners-up behind Isabella Wranaa's Swede's. Alina Paetz, who won world and European gold in 2023, led her Swiss to five straight wins to top of Group A ahead of Evelina Barone's Latvians. [BBC] New-look Scottish rinks eye European curling medals - watch live on BBC

item.title: ‘That’s not right’ – Jerry Jones called out by Super Bowl winner over Troy Aikman suggestion
item.description: Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images Troy Aikman’s future with ESPN is looking less and less certain by the day with some suggesting the Dallas Cowboys should look to bring him back into the building. The extent of Aikman’s debacle with ESPN continues to come to light with new revelations being shared by the media almost daily. Given his contract expires at the end of the season, it now feels unlikely that a deal will be agreed to keep him on Monday Night Football. Jerry Jones was spotted speaking to Aikman ahead of the Cowboys’ Monday Night Football victory over the Philadelphia Eagles recently. This has sparked suggestions that something could be in the works between the pair to bring Aikman back to Dallas in the future. Jerry Jones questioned over possible Troy Aikman hire with Dallas Cowboys Former New England Patriots and Eagles cornerback Asante Samuel has hit out at Jones over potentially bringing back Aikman, but not Michael Irvin. The 60-year-old, Irvin, has also become a regular on ESPN but there has been no suggestion Jones wants him back at the Cowboys. “How can Jerry Jones hire Troy Aikman and not bring Michael Irvin along? That’s not right,” said Samuel on X. The issue Jones may have – if he wants Aikman with the Cowboys – is that there could be a number of different networks already looking to pounce on the former quarterback’s ESPN debacle. It has become very messy for Aikman, with his relationships at ESPN taking a real blow. There is also the possibility that the contract saga may also have pushed Aikman away from broadcasting. However, he is unlikely to find a role in the NFL that pays as highly as his ESPN gig did. Jones is notorious for not investing heavily in his staff. The billionaire has no issues paying his players, but he often draws the line at spending considerable money on his staff. This could certainly be an issue if he does want Aikman back in the building. item.title: What's the youth path to the USMNT? How U.S. Soccer wants to widen it
item.description: USA TODAY Sports spoke with the U.S. Soccer Federation and Major League Soccer about the state of the American youth game and the pipeline to the top following last summer’s World Cup. Since its Round of 16 finish, the USMNT has gone 4-0 in fall friendlies and plays next in the Concacaf Nations League two-legged November quarterfinal series against Haiti . The USA has been boosted by an influx of youth . We explore how to create opportunities for every young soccer player so they can find their personal path. Read Part 1: Three ways to improve a kid’s youth soccer experience from the beginning Part II: How does the path to the USMNT work, and how can we widen it? There are childhood moments to which we can point that define our sports careers. For Ali Curtis, now president of MLS NEXT Pro , one of them came when he was about 9. He was a top player at his age, and he tried out for a local team full of kids two years older than him. He remembers being told he wasn’t going to make the team, as he was too small or too young. “In your own mind, you're always probably a better player than you think you are,” he says, “but I thought I was one of the top players at the tryouts." Before Curtis left the soccer complex, someone directed him toward another team in Livonia, Michigan, which was about 40 minutes away from where he lived. He joined the team, which connected him back to his age group but had a competitive environment. “That was probably the most difficult moment that I had in my career or my soccer journey at the time,” he says. “But it happened to be the best thing that ever happened to me. I went and played for that team and was off to the races after that in terms of everything that happened in my youth soccer career and journey.” When he made a regional team at around 14, Curtis was required to go on an international trip. But his mother said they couldn’t afford it. Curtis, now 47, remembers his coaches finding a way to fund the trip, which cleared his pathway to a national team, and eventually, Major League Soccer , which began in 1996. As U.S. Soccer seeks to widen its pool of potential players, would Curtis emerge on the national radar today? His story covers at least two issues that are still rampant in youth soccer: high costs that limit access, and coaches' distorted eye toward players who may not be considered top-level on their teams but blossom later. U.S. Soccer is working with its state associations to create a more unified system that will lower costs, provide more meaningful experiences and grow participation. Its officials say it’s only at the beginning of this process. “There are many more people who can legitimately aspire to play professional men’s or women's soccer in the country than could even 15 years ago, a great asset for the growth of sport,” says Dan Helfrich, chief operating officer of the U.S. Soccer Federation. “And the existence of so many national and regional leagues and competitions that are different in the w

item.title: Connor McDavid's outrageous start creates historic Halloween showdown with NHL's newest young star
item.description: Connor McDavid's outrageous start creates historic Halloween showdown with NHL's newest young star originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Connor McDavid has produced extraordinary seasons throughout his NHL career, but his opening month of 2026-27 has reached a level that almost defies explanation. The Edmonton Oilers captain enters Saturday's game against the New York Islanders with 36 points in 13 games. That includes eight goals and 28 assists, giving him an average of more than 2.7 points per game. McDavid has also recorded an assist in every game Edmonton has played this season, establishing an NHL record for the longest assist streak to begin a campaign. His remarkable start has created a fascinating Halloween afternoon against one of hockey's most promising young players. Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NHL Draft, will share the ice with the player selected first overall a decade earlier. Two first overall picks, two different stages McDavid was the first pick in the 2015 NHL Draft and has spent the following decade becoming one of the most productive offensive players of his generation. Connor McDavid is good at hockey. https://t.co/FFSDKqYGjU — DraftKings Sports (@DKSports) October 30, 2026 Schaefer represents the next wave of elite talent. The young Islanders defenseman enters Saturday with 14 points in 13 games, including four goals and 10 assists. He also ranks third in the NHL in average ice time at 26 minutes, 58 seconds per game. That workload is particularly striking for a player so early in his professional career. McDavid leads NHL forwards in average ice time at 23 minutes, 30 seconds, making it likely that the two will see plenty of each other. The matchup offers a rare opportunity to watch an established superstar face a young defenseman already trusted with enormous responsibility. McDavid is chasing more than wins McDavid's 36 points put him on a mathematical pace for 232 points over an 82-game season. That is a projection, not a prediction. Maintaining such production for an entire season would be an extraordinary challenge. Still, the numbers demonstrate just how unusual his opening stretch has been. McDavid extended his record assist streak with two assists in Edmonton's 4-0 victory over Calgary on Wednesday. The Oilers enter Saturday with a 9-2-2 record and a franchise-record five consecutive road victories to begin a season. The Islanders are 7-4-2 and have won four of their last six games, including an overtime victory against Minnesota on Thursday. Schaefer scored the winner in that game. item.title: Is Georgia DB KJ Bolden playing vs. Florida? Latest injury update
item.description: The Georgia Bulldogs are expected to get back one of their top players for the Florida Gators game. After having a bye week to heal up, Georgia All-American and first-team All-SEC safety KJ Bolden is expected to return against Florida. Bolden is listed as questionable in the SEC's availability report , but is expected to play, per CBS Sports . Bolden was sidelined for Georgia's loss against Auburn due to a lower leg injury. The junior safety is a critical part of the Georgia defense. Bolden initially suffered the injury in the second half of Georgia's road win over the Alabama Crimson Tide . He may not be back to 100% for the Florida game, so it will be interesting to see what his role is. With Bolden out, Georgia primarily played Ja'Marley Riddle at safety. Kyron Jones and Zion Branch are other options Georgia has at safety opposite of starter Rasean Dinkins. Is KJ Bolden playing today? Bolden is questionable in the SEC availability report, which will be updated 90 minutes before kickoff. CBS reports that Bolden is expected to be available against Florida. Bolden has 22 tackles, one interception and three pass deflections this season. He plays a critical role in communication for Georgia's secondary. CBS Sports KJ Bolden update Georgia star safety KJ Bolden, who has been working back from a lower leg injury he suffered against Alabama Oct. 10, is currently expected to be available tomorrow when the No. 3 Bulldogs face No. 17 Florida, sources tell @CBSSports pic.twitter.com/kI5hCnQnjA — Matt Zenitz (@mzenitz) October 30, 2026 Follow UGA Wire on Instagram , Facebook , X (formerly Twitter) or Threads for more Georgia football coverage! item.title: Colts now open to trading Jonathan Taylor, Giants & Vikings among 5 teams to express interest
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts have reportedly changed their stance on trading star running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the trade deadline. The Colts were reportedly reluctant about trading their best player, but ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport report that the team is now willing to move him. “The Indianapolis Colts now are open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor, sources told ESPN and NFL Network,” Schefter and Rapoport wrote on Saturday morning. The NFL insiders added that “multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing, according to sources.” MORE: Wrestling legends loved Christian Watson’s WWE-style return That second part of the report suggests it might not be long before Taylor is moved. Perhaps we’ll see a trade go down after this weekend, but that obviously hasn’t been confirmed. It just makes sense for the Colts to move Taylor at this point. With the rebuild incoming, the Colts are at least a few years away from competing again and Taylor could start to decline in that span. His value may never be higher than it is now, so trading him is the logical move. 5 teams expressing interest in Taylor Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) rushes the ball against the Minnesota Vikings in the second half at U.S. Bank Stadium. Credit: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Included in the report is the five teams that have “expressed at least some level of interest” in Taylor. The list includes the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks. “The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor so far is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks, sources said,” the NFL insiders said. The Broncos already have a pretty crowded running backs room with RJ Harvey, J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman, but none of those guys are as talented as Taylor, of course. MORE: ESPN reportedly picks sides in Aikman-Bucks fallout The Giants might have the most dire need of that group, as they have Cam Skattebo and not much else in their running backs room. Minnesota is right there with them with their uninspiring group led by Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason. The Packers recently got back Josh Jacobs, but the veteran running back is now facing more allegations of abuse, according to ESPN , which leaves his outlook murky. Seattle has already swung a big trade with the Colts for Quenton Nelson and could certainly use an upgrade at running back, even with Jadarian Price set to return from injury. No matter where he lands, the former rushing champion is going to amount to a big upgrade. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Inside how Max Eberl knew Vincent Kompany was perfect for Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Sebastian El-Saqqa - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Vincent Kompany was not the obvious choice to succeed Thomas Tuchel at Bayern Munich. He had just suffered relegation with Burnley, and appointing him to lead one of the biggest clubs in world football was a gamble that raised p lenty of eyebrows. Yet, Max Eberl saw something in the Belgian coach that went far beyond the results on his CV. Now, with Kompany having restored Bayern’s attacking identity, revitalized the atmosphere around the squad, and established himself as one of the most exciting coaches in European football, Eberl has opened up about how the appointment came together in an interview with Säbener 51 (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). The initial conversation that changed everything Asked whether Kompany was his masterstroke signing, rather than a player, Eberl explained why the appointment would not necessarily have been an easy sell at the time. “I joined the club at a time when it was already cle ar that the coach would not continue beyond the end of the season. And now, looking back, I can say this: if I had presented Vincent Kompany as my very first choice, I don’t know what the reaction would have been ,” said Eberl. “The relegated Burnley manager as Thomas Tuchel’s successor?” Kompany was not the only candidate considered. Bayern explored several options, including Julian Nagelsmann and Ralf Rangnick, before Eberl decided to contact the former Manchester City captain. “Of cour se, we worked our way through a list of candidates. Julian Nagelsmann was one of them; that’ s no secret. I had a very good relationship with him, but he decided to take the Germany job. Ralf Rangnick al so went in a different direction,” Eberl stated. “We analyzed the market very carefully at the time, and everything we heard about Burnley’s young coach was positive. At some point, I said, ‘Right, I’m just going to give Vinnie a call.’ We spoke on the phone before our Champions League semi-final in Madrid. A fter four hours, I had to say, ‘Sorry, it’s 6 p.m. I have to g o to the team meeting.’ — I hung up and thought: Wow, this feels good! He’s a real character. Then I asked Christop h Freund to form his own opinion of him. He came back equally convinced.” Four hours on the phone was enough to leave a stron g impression on Eberl. Freund came away equally enthusiastic, but Bayern still needed to be convinced that Kompany’s relegation with Burnley did not tell the whole story. Why Bayern looked beyond Burnley’s relegation Kompany had led Burnley to promotion with 101 points before suffering relegation in the Premier League. For Bayern, however, the important question was not simply whether his previous team had stayed up. It was what his approach to football revealed about his potential. “Vinnie won promotion with Burnley w ith 101 points, only to be relegated again the following season. You could have looked at that and thought: He can’t get the job done; he can’t adapt. But we sa

The Red Devils are without a win in eight games as the pressure mounts on manager Michael Carrick, who has led United to its worst start to a campaign in 40 years. A 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth last weekend looked like it would be the nail in the coffin for Carrick, but a midweek meeting with United’s hierarchy saw him kept on. That being said, there’s a feeling he may be pushed from the plank sooner rather than later if the current malaise persists for much longer. Xabi Alonso could also do with a positive response from his side after going two without a win, losing 2-0 at home to Tottenham Hotspur before defeat at Liverpool on Wednesday saw the Blues booted from the Carabao Cup. Almost 18 months have passed since Chelsea last secured a win over United in May 2025, but Liverpool icon Alonso will have extra motivation to earn all three points against his old nemesis. Cole Palmer is back from suspension and should make an immediate return to Chelsea’s XI, especially with Joao Pedro unlikely to return until late November. item.title: Mets, Yankees Castoff Clay Holmes Cuts Ties With Cubs After Very Short Stint
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 22: Clay Holmes #25 of the Chicago Cubs looks on before a game against the Miami Marlins at Wrigley Field on September 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Isaac Wasserman/Getty Images) Getty Images The New York Mets and New York Yankees both enter the offseason with considerable questions after another disappointing year for the city’s two baseball franchises. The Mets missed the postseason for the second consecutive season following a blockbuster roster overhaul, while the Yankees suffered another early playoff exit, extending their championship drought and raising questions about deeper clubhouse problems Both organizations have important decisions to make about their rosters, and have opened the offseason with one familiar name suddenly becoming an intriguing option for either club. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Yankees Infielder Core Jackson Calls For Change With Team Fundamentals Under Fire Former New York Yankees, New York Mets Star Cuts Ties With Chicago Cubs After Just 9 Games On Thursday, news broke that Clay Holmes, who has experience with both New York franchises, has now returned to the open market. “Cubs off season will be busy on the mound,” ESPN’s Jesse Rogers reported . “Clay Holmes and Matthew Boyd are turning down their player options to become free agents.” While Boyd is a longtime Cubs contributor, Holmes’ departure from Chicago comes shortly after the 33-year-old was acquired from the Mets at the trade deadline. Ultimately, his stay in Chicago lasted just nine starts before he returned to the offseason market. Holmes was considerably more effective over the entire season than his abbreviated Cubs tenure might suggest. He finished with a 3.29 ERA, 1.19 WHIP and 78 strikeouts across 101.1 innings, though a fractured fibula limited him to 18 starts. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers Acquire Young Pitcher Alberto Santos Right Before Free Agency Opens Could New York Yankees Or New York Mets Pursue Clay Holmes Reunion? Despite the lower-body injury, Holmes’ overall performance gives him a reasonable case for another opportunity in a major-league rotation. After his decision to leave the Cubs, Chicago will still get the chance to pitch him on a new contract first, but he’s more than likely to decline any initial overtures. “The Cubs will have an exclusive negotiating window with Holmes for a few days, and they are reportedly interested in re-signing the righty,” CBS Sports noted . “However, Holmes is almost surely going to reach free agency and field bids from several clubs.” Holmes has an established history in New York, having spent four seasons with the Yankees before joining the Mets ahead of the 2025 campaign. He initially made his name as a high-leverage reliever in the Bronx, recording 74 saves between 2022 and 2024. The Mets subsequently signed him to a three-year, $38 million contract with the intention of converting him into a starting pitcher. That transition initially worked well, as Holmes

item.title: Trans player Julie Tetart goes viral after dominating top WNBA prospect
item.description: Photo by Valery HACHE / AFP via Getty Images Anyone saying Julie Tetart can’t hang with WNBA talent just got proved wrong. French big Julie Tetart has quickly turned into one of the most talked-about names, and she makes no secret of her admiration for the WNBA. The 6-foot-3 post currently tears it up for Monaco Basket Association in France’s second tier, putting up impressive numbers under the rim. Having played in the men’s leagues prior to her transition, she was cleared to play women’s pro ball and hasn’t looked back. However, it’s unlikely that we’ll see her in the WNBA anytime soon, as Cathy Engelbert has rejected Enes Kanter’s draft advances due to him not being a biological female. Julie Tetart dominates WNBA prospect Ainhoa Risacher OutKick editor Joe Kinsey sparked intense debate online after shining a spotlight on Julie Tetart’s head-to-head showdown with a top French talent. His post received over 475k views. Framing the matchup as a direct answer to critics who doubt the French trans centre could ever hold her own stateside, Kinsey pointed to her performance against a projected 2027 lottery pick, Ainhoa Risacher. The actual match, a Coupe de France clash, saw Lyon ASVEL outlast Monaco 81–71. On an individual level, Tetart was everywhere on the floor, racking up 13 points, 9 rebounds, 5 steals, and 2 blocks. Meanwhile, Ainhoa Risacher had nine points alongside 6 assists, 6 steals and 6 boards. Ainhoa Risacher is the younger sister of NBA number-one pick Zaccharie Risacher. item.title: Cannavaro: ‘Spalletti and Allegri are similar, Kolo Muani and Hojlund less killer than strikers of my era’
item.description: Cannavaro: ‘Spalletti and Allegri are similar, Kolo Muani and Hojlund less killer than strikers of my era’ Fabio Cannavaro believes Luciano Spalletti and Massimiliano Allegri have plenty in common, and that Rasmus Højlund and Randal Kolo Muani are not the ruthless strikers of his generation. With quotes via Calciomercato.com , the former defender, who played for both clubs, previewed Sunday’s clash between Juventus and Napoli in an interview with Betsson.Sport. It kicks off at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT] at the Allianz Stadium. “Spalletti and Allegri are two great coaches who have achieved great results in recent years,” Cannavaro said. “They know Italian football very well and everything that surrounds it: how to manage players, journalists and fans. Tactically, they’re not tied to one system and they know how to adapt to their players.” Allegri will not be on the touchline. He is serving the second game of a two-match ban, so assistant Marco Landucci takes charge again. The sides go into the game level on 14 points, but in very different moods. Napoli won 4-1 at Monza on Wednesday, while Juventus were beaten 2-0 at Genoa. Spalletti apologised to the fans after that defeat. “Napoli have certainly paid for a few too many injuries at the start of the season, while Juve, who have changed more than last year, can’t find consistency,” Cannavaro said. “Both Gasperini and Chivu have worked with their groups, so this year we’re seeing the results.” NAPLES, ITALY – JANUARY 13: Massimiliano Allegri Juventus coach greets Luciano Spalletti SSC Napoli coach before the Serie A match between SSC Napoli_Juventus at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on January 13, 2023 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Cannavaro on Bremer, Buongiorno and the strikers Cannavaro won the Ballon d’Or in 2006 as a Juventus player, and he was full of praise for both sides’ centre-backs. “I really like Buongiorno because he’s a real defender. He senses danger, he knows when to step up and when to be hard,” he said. “The same goes for Bremer, they’re two extraordinary players. Both always have a lot of injuries, but they’re fundamental for Juve and Napoli.” Alessandro Buongiorno is out until the new year after knee surgery, while Gleison Bremer is a doubt for Sunday. Football today is much faster, more intense and more athletic,” he said. “Strikers from my generation were a bit more ‘killer’ in front of goal. Nowadays strikers play more for the team and work a lot off the ball.” The Neapolitan, who grew up in Fuorigrotta in the shadow of the San Paolo, also looked back on his Napoli debut. “I think it was the mo

item.title: Wyndham Clark’s comments about his brother suggest why he missed the cut at the Mexico Open
item.description: Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images Wyndham Clark’s family affair at the Mexico Open did not go to plan. The two-time US Open winner had his brother on the bag in Mexico and hoped to help pay for his wedding with the prize money. Instead, Clark missed the cut by two strokes in one of his worst performances of the season. Clark has been in fine form of late and is in the midst of a bounce back season, so this week was an anomaly. But what he said about his brother in the week’s build-up is a clue as to what happened to his golf game. Wyndham Clark criticized his brother’s caddying ability Clark lost 3.31 strokes to the field on approach, and 1.43 strokes to the field with his putting. These are the two areas of the game where caddying matters most, and they cost Clark in Mexico. That is hardly surprising, considering Clark admitted his brother gave him the wrong yardages the last time he caddied for him at Colonial. Speaking to SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio in the build-up to the Mexico Open, he said, “He ChatGPT’d the stats of the golf course and looked it up relative to my stats, but what was funny is they changed the routing of the golf course, added new holes, so all that went out the window. “He was trying to do all this hard work, and none of it was going to help.” It’s hard to know whether Clark’s performance was down to poor caddying or whether he just missed putts and his swing was off, but judging by his comments about his brother, he really could have done with a professional caddie on the bag. item.title: WNBA Finals Game 7 gives Golden State chance to complete one of basketball's most remarkable expansion stories
item.description: WNBA Finals Game 7 gives Golden State chance to complete one of basketball's most remarkable expansion stories originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Valkyries have already accomplished something no other WNBA expansion franchise has managed. On Saturday night, they have an opportunity to do something even more extraordinary. Golden State hosts the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals at Chase Center, with both franchises seeking their first championship. The deciding game comes less than two years after the Valkyries began their inaugural season. For a franchise that was still introducing itself to professional basketball fans in 2025, the possibility of raising a championship trophy in 2026 is almost difficult to comprehend. And the most remarkable part of Golden State's rise is how quickly it has happened. From expansion team to championship contender The Valkyries made history during their first season by becoming the first WNBA expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in its inaugural year. Instead of treating that accomplishment as a long-term building block, Golden State immediately took another step. IT ALL COMES DOWN TO THIS 🚨 Saturday. A winner-take-all Game 7. 🏆 8pm/ET | USA Network & Peacock | #WNBASeason30 https://t.co/B8LdnAFtEG — WNBA (@WNBA) October 29, 2026 The Valkyries finished the 2026 regular season with a 32-12 record, earning the No. 2 seed and improving by nine victories over their first season. Their defense became the foundation of their success, while their roster depth allowed them to compete against more established teams. Golden State survived a difficult first-round series against the Dallas Wings before sweeping the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals. That victory made the Valkyries the only expansion franchise in league history to reach the Finals in its second season. Now they are one game away from turning that achievement into a championship. Atlanta has its own remarkable opportunity The Dream have no intention of becoming a footnote in Golden State's story. Atlanta forced Game 7 with an 80-69 victory Thursday, using a dominant opening quarter to prevent the Valkyries from celebrating a title on the road. Allisha Gray scored 23 points, Rhyne Howard added 21 and Angel Reese delivered another double-double. Atlanta led by as many as 25 points before surviving a late Golden State rally. The Dream are also pursuing their first championship, making the stakes historic regardless of the winner. Golden State's Gabby Williams scored 26 points in Game 6 and remains a central figure in the Valkyries' title hopes. MORE : Sophie Cunningham’s message to women after F1 appearance is about more than height A championship nobody can take away The WNBA expanded its Finals to a best-of-seven format in 2025, making Saturday's contest the first Game 7 in league championship history. That guarantees a new kind of moment

item.title: Kimi Antonelli Doesn't Miss Normal University Life While Friends Study and Work
item.description: Kimi Antonelli is not envious of his friends living a simpler life. (Source: MEGA) All but certain to be crowned the F1 world champion this weekend in Mexico City, Kimi Antonelli is living a life most would only dream of at 20. Now the second youngest driver on the current grid after Arvid Lindblad , most of Antonelli’s friends are off to work their jobs or pursue higher studies in their respective domains. And while some people might miss the simpler pleasures of life, the Mercedes driver doesn’t. With Antonelli’s fame growing almost as quickly as he drives on the track, Antonelli understands that the attention could quickly become suffocating for him. And when The Telegraph UK quizzed him on whether he envies his friends from school, the Italian was clear with his words. Kimi Antonelli on missing out on a normal university life while his friends study, work and enjoy their weekends: "Not really, to be fair. I really love the life I do." "Once you grow up and you become sure of what you want to do in life, you're also willing to make these… pic.twitter.com/fryYsNxZrB — Everything Formula (@evrythngformu1a) October 30, 2026 “Not really, to be fair. I really love the life I do.” He added, “If you would have asked me this question when I was 10,11, I would have probably said, ‘maybe I’ll miss it.’ But once you grow up and become sure of what you want to do in life, then, you know, you’re also willing to make these sacrifices.” For Antonelli, perhaps the only thing he’ll miss is the privacy. When stepping out of the house or going to the restaurant, the Italian knows that he won’t be able to relax, given that a camera would always be pointing at him. But other than that, he has no issues. Kimi Antonelli Has Still Found a Way To Keep Things Fun at Work With work consuming most of his life now, the 20-year-old needs time to enjoy life as well. With friends, the luxury of having fun becomes undervalued, but at work, the young driver understands its importance. Given this, the soon-to-be F1 world champion has found a way to unwind while still working. Kimi Antonelli has found a way to keep things fun at work with his pranks. (Source: MEGA) He has retained a youthful love for pranks, with his race engineer Peter ‘Bono’ Bonnington bearing most of the brunt. One such prank came during the pre-season testing, when Antonelli secretly put chili sauce in Bono’s drink. A follow-up came when Bono was soaked with a water gun by the young driver, giving way to a sort of war between the two teammates. The third chapter of the prank wars came when Antonelli ended up convincing the security staff at Brackley to disable Bono’s access card. The prank war between Kimi and Bono started after this pic.twitter.com/QR9y2MB3Xp — out of context Peter Bonnington (@bonotires) October 31, 2026 But as things stand, it is the Mercedes team that had the last laugh, luring Antonelli in for a fake interview before ambushing him with plates of whipped cream to celebrate his 20th birth

item.title: 'Rolls-Royce of bowling': Kagiso Rabada hailed as he completes 350 Test wickets in Day of 3rd Test vs Australia
item.description: 'Rolls-Royce of bowling': Kagiso Rabada hailed as he completes 350 Test wickets in Day of 3rd Test vs Australia originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: South Africa star Kagiso Rabada reached 350 Test wickets on the final day at Newlands. He got there in 13,808 balls, fewer than any bowler in history. Rabada took two wickets in the first over of Australia 's chase. Rabada reaches 350 and takes Dale Steyn's record with him Australia began the final day at Newlands needing 288 to win the series, and the first over told them how it was going to go. Kagiso Rabada had Matt Renshaw caught behind by Ryan Rickelton off the third ball and trapped Marnus Labuschagne lbw three balls later, the review offering no reprieve. The milestone arrived in his fourth over. Travis Head went for 14, caught by Marco Jansen, and Rabada had his 350th Test wicket with Australia 20 for 3 and the celebrations starting around him. The number that matters most is the one beside it. Rabada needed 13,808 deliveries to reach 350, which is fewer than any bowler has taken, and the man he moved past is Dale Steyn on 14,719. He becomes the fourth South African to the mark, behind Steyn on 439, Shaun Pollock on 421 and Makhaya Ntini on 390. By matches, the 31-year-old got there in his 75th Test, second only to Steyn's 69 among South Africans and level with Malcolm Marshall on the all-time pace list. The same spell also made him the fifth South African to 600 international wickets, a tally that now stands at 601 from 260 matches. MORE: Last Australian captain to win Test series in South Africa: Full list as Pat Cummins faces Steve Smith's fate Cricket world reacts to Rabada's 350th Test wicket The reaction began with the comparison South African supporters reach for when Rabada is running in with a new ball. "The Rolls Royce of South African bowling. KAGISO RABADA!" Mondli Thwala wrote , posting it alongside an animation of the Rolls-Royce hood ornament. The Rolls Royce of South African bowling #SAvAUS KAGISO RABADA! — Mondli Thwala (@mondli_thwala) October 31, 2026 Others went to the scorecard, where three of Australia's top four had already gone back. "Rabada breathing fire at Newlands and picking up all three," one posted , noting that he was the second-fastest South African to the landmark by matches played. Kagiso Rabada officially crossed the major landmark of 350 Test wickets, becoming the 2nd fastest South African to reach the milestone in Test match history. The top 3 are completely dismantled! Rabada breathing fire at Newlands and picking up all three — (@Wildfire4lg) October 31, 2026 The sharpest point was about what the number might have been. "If South Africa played as much Test cricket as England or Australia do, Kagiso Rabada would comfortably have 600 Test wickets by now," one supporter argued . Auburn's stunning 27-24 triumph in Athens two weeks ago not only knocked UGA out of the top spot in the polls; it also represented Georgia's first loss to an unranked team since October 2019, when the Bulldogs fell at home to South Carolina. Given a bye week to tinker with what went wrong, Smart undoubtedly will have his charges out for blood as they face No. 17 Florida in an unusual venue. For the first time in a rivalry that dates back more than a century, Georgia and Florida will face off in Atlanta, as the series has been relocated from its traditional home in Jacksonville for two years due to stadium renovations. The Gators should enter the game flying high on the heels of a huge upset of then-No. 7 Texas in Austin before their bye week. Then again, it's difficult to predict which Florida team will show up — that version or the Gators who were handled easily by South Carolina and Missouri the previous two weeks. item.title: Liverpool star wanted by two clubs in January move
item.description: Liverpool star wanted by two clubs in January move Federico Chiesa transfer latest as Liverpool weigh January exit Liverpool’s forward line has shifted quickly in recent months and Federico Chiesa now looks like one of the clearest names facing an uncertain future. With Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz added after Mohamed Salah’s departure, and with Alexander Isak back in form, competition in the attacking unit has intensified under Andoni Iraola. That leaves Chiesa in a difficult position. The Italy international arrived from Juventus in 2024 for £12.5 million, but his spell at Anfield has never truly gathered momentum. Fitness issues, disrupted availability and a lack of sustained rhythm have all played their part. Even when chances have come, he has struggled to establish himself in a crowded attacking picture that also includes Hugo Ekitike, Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas. According to Tuttomercato , AC Milan and Lazio have now made enquiries over Chiesa’s situation, while Inter remain attentive after previous interest. The latest reporting suggests Liverpool are expected to hold discussions with the player over what comes next, including the possibility of a move in the January window. AC Milan and Lazio make Chiesa enquiries There is a clear sense that any deal would be shaped by market conditions in Italy. A permanent transfer may prove difficult immediately, particularly given the player’s salary and Liverpool’s need to protect value. For that reason, an initial loan with an option to buy appears the most realistic structure being explored by potential suitors. Photo IMAGO That model would give interested clubs some protection around Chiesa’s fitness record, while also allowing Liverpool to move the situation forward without becoming locked in prolonged negotiations over a full fee. Inter’s stance may also depend on movement elsewhere, with their long-running Luis Henrique situation still relevant to any attacking reshuffle. Liverpool squad depth raises January questions For Liverpool, this increasingly feels like a practical squad-management issue. Chiesa’s contract runs until June 2028, but the wider context matters more than the paperwork. If minutes remain limited and opportunities narrow further, a January solution could suit all parties. A return to Serie A is gathering momentum. Whether that becomes AC Milan, Lazio or Inter may depend on finances more than preference, but the direction of travel looks increasingly clear. Our View This has felt inevitable for a while. Chiesa arrived with genuine quality and pedigree, and there was real excitement about what he could offer, but Liverpool have barely seen a run of games that allowed him to settle. Every time there looked to be a window for him, something got in the way, whether that was injury, timing or simply the team moving on without him. item.title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs Has More Abuse Claims Emerge in New Records
item.description: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs. Getty The NFL is still reviewing whether to take disciplinary action against Josh Jacobs. Getty Josh Jacobs has played in the past two games for the Packers. Getty New records show that additional women have accused Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs of abuse in the months since his initial May 2026 arrest following a domestic altercation with his former girlfriend, according to NBC 26. The Green Bay-based NBC 26 reported late Friday night that three more women have contacted police to make abuse allegations against Jacobs for prior incidents, citing “a heavily redacted Hobart/Lawrence Police Department case file” that they obtained. According to NBC 26, the first of the three additional women came forward in June 2026 after learning of the investigation into Jacobs’ more recent incident, “telling police the allegations sounded similar to her prior experience with Jacobs” in 2022. Per NBC 26: “According to the records, the woman alleged Jacobs slapped her across the face and later took her cellphone as she attempted to leave his residence. The woman told investigators that Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down and later threw her onto the floor. The woman also alleged Jacobs spit on her and grabbed her by the throat. “The woman told police she initially met Jacobs through Instagram and communicated with him for approximately six months prior to meeting him in person. She said she remained friends with him for some time after the incident and did not want to report him.” Records Show 3 Women Reported Josh Jacobs After Arrest The records that NBC 26 obtained also detailed accounts from two other women who contacted the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department to report alleged physical incidents involving Jacobs during its investigation into his recent incident over the summer. One accused Jacobs of physically abusing her during an argument in April 2021: “The woman told the Hobart/Lawrence police that she called the police at the time. She said she later contacted the unnamed police department and said she was told it was not being investigated as a domestic incident because she and Jacobs were not in a relationship at the time. The records released to NBC 26 say detectives with the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department received records from that call. Those records indicated responding officers observed no visible signs of injury, bruising, or damage consistent with a physical altercation.” The third woman alleged that Jacobs “placed his hands on her head and neck, dragged her, scratched her chest, and took possession of her cell phone after it fell to the floor,” which she claimed left her with bruising and scratches for about a month, per NBC 26. “The woman told Hobart/Lawrence Police she did not report the incident to police or seek medical treatment at the time. item.title: Isack Hadjar Shoves Fan in Mexico GP Paddock as F1 Fans Debate His Behavior
item.description: Isack Hadjar is in a spot of bother after a video emerged from the F1 Mexico GP showing him shoving a fan, who was trying to take a selfie with him. Ever since his showing in Baku, Red Bull’s Hadjar has been in a spot of bother in the F1 races in Malaysia, Singapore and Austin. He has scored some points in the races, but the Frenchman has lacked pace against Max Verstappen . To add, with the car troubles, whether it is the radio or his clutch, Hadjar has been candid about the issues faced and urged Red Bull to rectify and redesign. “I mean we will keep pushing to that end,” he said ahead of the F1 Mexico GP weekend. Hadjar Tones Down on Austin Criticism “It’s something we’ve been working on and there have definitely been big improvements if you look at the first couple of races of the year. And now we’re at a point where it goes a bit up and down, but we are aware of that, and we need to work with what we have until the end of the year. “But the good thing is, going fast on track, I think we’re doing it. I think we also got a bit wrong on the strategy; it’s been reviewed. And yeah, we move forward, but yeah, I wouldn’t say they are silly things. I would say they are important little things that we don’t do well. That’s it. “Fortunately, I didn’t really think [about what I said in Austin]. I don’t think I really know, to be honest, as well. With myself, I still have stuff I should have kept for myself for sure. And I know that, and that’s it,” summed up Hadjar. (Photo by Alastair Staley/LAT Images) // Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610300453 // Usage for editorial use only // What Happened with Hadjar in the Paddock A week on from that, the Frenchman is again making headlines for the wrong reasons. A power unit issue hampered him in FP1 of the F1 Mexico GP. He was quite vocal on the radio. But Red Bull managed to get him out, as he ended up 11th. He followed it up with a sixth-place finish in FP2. However, what transpired between the two sessions caught the social media eye. A small clip showed Hadjar walking towards his Red Bull garage when a fan tried to grab him for a selfie. He tried to stop him by raising his hands, but when the fan didn’t budge, Hadjar pushed him away. The clip went viral, and the FIA took note of the same. The Frenchman got a summons from the stewards for alleged misconduct. Se enojó Hadjar #f1 . @F1 https://t.co/nnRyyHntiV — 1F #MexicoGP (@1FMasters) October 30, 2026 The FIA reckons he is in breach of Article 12.2.1.l of the FIA International Sporting Code – Misconduct relating to an incident in the Formula 1 Paddock. Hadjar has to visit the stewards on Saturday at 10:15 local time to explain his actions. He is the third Red Bull driver to visit the office after penalties for Verstappen and Liam Lawson . item.title: Red Sox Star's World Series Celebration Reveals Bigger Story Behind Brewers Title
item.description: Red Sox Star's World Series Celebration Reveals Bigger Story Behind Brewers Title originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox were not part of the 2026 World Series, but one of their most recognizable players had a reason to celebrate when the Milwaukee Brewers won the championship. Willson Contreras watched from the stands at Tropicana Field as his younger brother, William Contreras, helped Milwaukee capture the first World Series title in franchise history. For the Red Sox slugger, the moment was about considerably more than baseball. William earned World Series MVP honors after batting .381 with four RBIs during Milwaukee's five-game victory over the Tampa Bay Rays. Willson, wearing his brother's Brewers jersey, celebrated from the crowd before joining his family on the field. The images provided one of the most personal moments of the championship celebration. A Different Kind Of October Victory The Contreras brothers have spent years establishing themselves as major league players, each developing a reputation as a competitive and emotional presence. Willson Contreras watching his brother William win the world series 🥹 https://t.co/BS0T9ux6aA — Baseball Quotes (@BaseballQuotes1) October 29, 2026 William's championship represented the biggest achievement of his career. For Willson, the celebration offered something that cannot be measured by his own statistics or Boston's postseason finish. He was able to watch his younger brother reach the top of the sport. MLB shared footage of Willson reacting to Milwaukee's victory, followed by scenes of the family celebrating together. It was a reminder that the World Series is not always just about the players wearing the uniforms on the field. Sometimes the most meaningful reaction comes from someone who understands exactly how difficult reaching that moment can be. The Boston Connection Goes Beyond Family Willson's celebration also arrived during an interesting offseason for the Red Sox. Boston's season ended with a Wild Card Series defeat against the New York Yankees, followed by pointed comments from Contreras about the organization's leadership. Those comments raised questions about his relationship with the club entering 2027. But Contreras subsequently met with chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and manager Chad Tracy. In comments reported by the Boston Globe, Contreras acknowledged the frustration that followed the playoff exit and indicated that the sides had reached a better understanding. That distinction matters. The emotional reaction to losing in Boston and the emotional reaction to watching his brother win in Milwaukee came from the same player, but under very different circumstances. item.description: Bournemouth v Manchester City - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Paris Saint-Germain are closely monitoring Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi as he makes his return from a long-term foot injury. The French side face stiff competition from a host of Premier League heavyweights, including Arsenal and Manchester United, who are all circling the talented youngster. Kroupi returns to Bournemouth action PSG and a host of top European clubs are keeping a close eye on Bournemouth forward Kroupi following his long-awaited return to first-team action. The 20-year-old has recently recovered from a fractured fifth metatarsa l in his right foot, a severe injury he unfortunately sustained in July. After spending three gruelling months in the treatment room, the France Under-21 international is finally taking the necessary steps to rebuild his match fitness. Bournemouth manager Marco Rose is currently managing his minutes carefully, ensuring he does not rush the highly-rated youngster back onto the pitch too quickly. He made a brief cameo during Sunday's impressive 3-0 victory against Manchester United at Old Trafford. Kroupi then followed that up with another substitute appearance in a 3-0 League Cup triumph over Aston Villa three days later. European giants circle the Cherries While Bournemouth are taking a patient, methodical approach with their young forward's recovery, his numerous suitors are showing far less restraint. Kroupi was already generating significant interest across Europe during the summer transfer window before his unfortunate foot injury halted any potential move. According to TEAMtalk , PSG and Barcelona are both continuing to monitor his progress closely now that he has officially returned to the pitch. They are joined by Premier League sides Chelsea and Tottenham, who remain incredibly keen on securing his signature in the near future. The race for the former Lorient player is rapidly heating up. Recent reports indicate that Arsenal and Manchester United have also formally added his name to their respective transfer shortlists. Bournemouth refuse winter transfer sale Despite the mounting transfer interest from some of Europe's most powerful clubs, Bournemouth are fully aware of Kroupi's immense value to their squad. The Cherries are completely opposed to letting their star attacking prospect leave the club during the upcoming winter window. Sitting 13th in the Premier League table, the south-coast outfit view the Frenchman as a crucial component for the remainder of the current campaign. They are absolutely determined to keep the door firmly shut on any January negotiations, regardless of the financial offers presented. PSG explore alternative targets Bournemouth's staunch refusal to sanction a sale in January presents a significant hurdle for PSG's immediate transfer plans. item.title: France's Nunez warns of high risk during protests
item.description: France is bracing for a third consecutive weekend of protests, with around 70,000 security personnel deployed to prevent a repeat of the violence seen on October 17. Shops have boarded up their premises as authorities warn of further clashes, with Halloween celebrations adding to security concerns over masked demonstrators. The protests, involving Yellow Vest activists, trade unions and students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality and poor school conditions, but have since expanded to include demands for greater civil liberties and the right to protest. The demonstrations come six months ahead of presidential elections, amid a tense political climate and growing support for the far right. Authorities have restricted marches in several cities, while Paris police have only authorised a demonstration on the capital's outskirts. Curfews have also been imposed in parts of Paris as officials seek to prevent further unrest.

item.title: Liverpool vs Arsenal: Classic match - Andrey Arshavin scores four in 4-4 Anfield draw
item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Relive the breathless drama of April 2009, when Andrey Arshavin struck four times at Anfield to dent Liverpool's Premier League title ambitions in a remarkable 4-4 draw. Braces from Fernando Torres and Yossi Benayoun rescued a late point for Rafael Benitez's side, yet the night belonged to Arsenal's clinical Russian forward. There are rare nights under the Anfield floodlights when tactical orthodoxy dissolves into pure, unscripted theatre. In April 2009, with the Premier League title race reaching breaking point, 44,424 spectators witnessed an eight-goal duel that defied all defensive logic. Watched from the stands by Liverpool's joint owners Tom Hicks and George Gillett, two of England's great heavyweights traded blows until neither side could stand. The siege of Anfield and the Russian twist The siege of Anfield and the Russian twist Without their talismanic captain Steven Gerrard, Benitez's side still began with ferocious intent, pinning Arsene Wenger's visitors deep inside their own half. Spearheaded by a relentless Torres, the hosts laid siege to goal, only to find an unlikely barrier in Lukasz Fabianski. Heavily criticised after an FA Cup semi-final defeat just days earlier, the Polish keeper produced an inspired first-half display, twice denying Torres before palming away Benayoun's drive. Football, however, rarely rewards dominance without ruthlessness. Nine minutes before the interval, Javier Mascherano was caught in possession, allowing Samir Nasri and Cesc Fabregas to carve open the home defence for Arshavin to crash a finish off the underside of the bar. Backed by a wall of sound from the Kop after the break, Liverpool overturned the deficit within eleven minutes. Dirk Kuyt turned creator twice, crossing for Torres to power home a 49th-minute header before finding Benayoun at the far post to loop a brave finish beyond Fabianski. Four-goal fury and stoppage-time salvation Four-goal fury and stoppage-time salvation Just as Anfield sensed victory, the lavishly gifted Arshavin turned tormentor across three mid-half minutes. In the 67th minute, the Russian robbed a hesitant Alvaro Arbeloa to flash a stunning 20-yard drive past Pepe Reina, before capitalising on Fabio Aurelio's sliced clearance to slot home Arsenal's third. Yet the chaos barely paused; within two minutes, Torres spun sharply to equalise once more, and only Kieran Gibbs clearing off the line denied the Spaniard a treble. With time expiring, Liverpool threw caution to the wind and suffered a classic sucker punch. From a home corner in the 90th minute, substitute Theo Walcott led a blistering counter-attack to tee up Arshavin for an emphatic fourth. Defeat loomed until deep into five frantic minutes of stoppage time, when Benayoun scrambled the ball home in a crowded area to salvage a 4-4 draw, before referee Howard Webb ignored a final handball shout against Abou Diaby. item.title: What We Heard Week 9: DI HC calls Michigan OC Jason Beck ‘exceptional’
item.description: Michigan offensive coordinator Jason Beck looks on before the spring game at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, April 18, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After today, the Michigan Wolverines will be three quarters of the way through their regular season, and many would say that they have regressed as a team and a program since Kyle Whittingham took over. Despite claims that he would right the ship and be the adult in the room, there are serious questions today about the legitimacy coaching style both on and off the field to return the maize and blue to the top of the Big Ten. A game against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights on Saturday afternoon has no business being close with Rutgers expecting to be down their starting quarterback and first-round talent at wide receiver. Throughout the week, seemingly everyone had an opinion to share about Whittingham, offensive coordinator Jason Beck, and the state of this program. Here’s what we heard this week as we trudge through the second half of the season. HC’s Take: Utah State HC Bronco Mendenhall sings the praises of Jason Beck It’s a clip that you have to see to believe that it was actually said. Bronco Mendenhall, the sitting head coach at Utah State, put his neck on the line for Beck, his former player and assistant. Bronco Mendenhall thinks the idea that Michigan Wolverines OC Jason Beck suddenly can’t coach is “asinine.” The Utah State head coach joined DJ & PK and defended his former player and offensive coordinator while acknowledging the pressure to deliver immediate results in college… pic.twitter.com/rKgN3TBJhD — KSL Sports (@kslsports) October 26, 2026 “The thought that now he can’t coach is just, excuse my language, asinine. Devin Gardner GOES OFF on Whittingham’s postgame comments: “I’m not surprised… this is just the latest edition of things our head coach has said that don’t sound like what we should expect… two years after a national championship.” pic.twitter.com/h5mcDJdEFP — Isaac Meyers (@meyersmedia_) October 26, 2026 “What have we seen from Coach Whittingham? item.title: 'I was on the bench': Yaxel Lendeborg says how he really felt after Steph Curry dropped Luka Doncic
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Steph Curry dropping Luka Doncic to the floor was the highlight of the Golden State Warriors’ NBA Cup win against the Los Angeles Lakers. The two superstars went head-to-head at the Chase Centre in San Francisco, and despite early dominance from the visitors, the hosts sealed a great win in the end. Everybody is talking about Curry’s ankle-breaker on Doncic, including the Slovenian’s new rival, Yaxel Lendeborg. Yaxel Lendeborg says he was ‘very happy’ to see Steph Curry drop Luka Doncic Lendeborg and Doncic formed a sudden rivalry that nobody expected in the first game of the season. The rookie and the superstar had a go at each other after Lendeborg took issue with Doncic complaining to the officials too much. The former even went on to say he lost respect for the Lakers icon. Since then, there has been a lot of hype heading into the Golden State Warriors’ NBA Cup game against the Los Angeles Lakers, all because of this newfound rivalry. Doncic won the individual battle on the floor, but Lendeborg has had the last laugh – not just because the Warriors won the game but also because Curry embarrassed the Slovenian. Unsurprisingly, after the game, Lendeborg was asked for his reaction to the incident, and he admitted that it made him happy. He said, as per KNBR : “It was amazing to watch. I was on the bench with my fourth foul, I think, but it was amazing to see. I was very happy about it. I’m happy big bro handled it.” We’re sure this will add a bit more fuel to the Yaxel-Luka drama, but Lendeborg was really poor where it mattered on Friday night – on the floor. The rookie managed just six points and one rebound in 24 minutes, which is his worst return for the Warriors since he made his debut on opening night. It remains to be seen how he will bounce back when Golden State take on the Clippers on Sunday night. item.title: Kentucky Basketball vs. Manhattan preview, viewing info, and prediction for stream-only game
item.description: Kentucky Basketball finished exhibition play with a perfect 3-0 record after defeating UCF, 90-76, in overtime on Wednesday. At times, the Wildcats looked like the better team but struggled to pull away from the Knights. UCF eventually took the lead in the final minutes of regulation before Kentucky guard Alex Wilkins hit a game-tying shot to send the contest into overtime. Kentucky then dominated the extra period, outscoring UCF 14-5. The performance showed that if the Wildcats can put everything together, they have the potential to be one of the better teams in the country. They demonstrated that potential earlier with a 76-65 victory over Texas Tech. Against UCF, four Wildcats reached double figures: Milan Momcilovic, Malachi Moreno, Mason Williams and Alex Wilkins. Kentucky will now turn its attention to the regular season, beginning Tuesday, Nov. 3, against Manhattan at 7 p.m. ET inside Rupp Arena as the Wildcats look to start their pursuit of a ninth national championship. This is also a pivotal third season for head coach Mark Pope. After Kentucky’s season ended with a second-round loss to Iowa State in the NCAA Tournament last year, expectations are high, and many believe this season could be a make-or-break year for Pope and the program. Manhattan, meanwhile, is coming off a difficult 2025-26 season in which the Jaspers finished 12-20. The program has also experienced significant roster turnover, returning only five of the 18 players from last season’s roster. Getting to know Manhattan John Gallagher enters his fourth season as Manhattan’s head coach in 2026-27. He was named the 24th head coach in program history on March 29, 2023, and brings 26 years of collegiate coaching experience at the Division I level. Before arriving at Manhattan, Gallagher spent 12 seasons as the head coach at Hartford, leading the Hawks to three postseason appearances. His tenure included an NCAA Tournament berth in 2021 after Hartford won the America East Championship. The Hawks faced eventual national champion Baylor in the first round. Gallagher also led Hartford to a program-record 19 wins during the 2017-18 season and helped the team reach consecutive America East championship games in 2019-20 and 2020-21. At Manhattan, Gallagher oversaw a significant turnaround during the 2024-25 season, leading the Jaspers to 17 wins, their highest total since 2014-15. The team earned the No. 5 seed in the Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference tournament and received an invitation to the College Basketball Invitational, where it lost to Incarnate Word in the first round. Now, Manhattan faces another challenge heading into 2026-27 after losing much of its roster from last season. Here’s what you need to watch for as the Kentucky Wildcats begin their quest for No. 9 on Tuesday. Kentucky needs a complete performance Although this is Kentucky’s first regular-season game, the Wildcats have already shown what their offense and defense can look like through three exhibition games.

item.title: Cardinale: ‘I’ll be devastated if Milan don’t win the derby, Amorim was a great choice’
item.description: Cardinale: ‘I’ll be devastated if Milan don’t win the derby, Amorim was a great choice’ Gerry Cardinale admits he will be “devastated” if Milan fail to beat Inter tonight, and has given Rúben Amorim his full backing after Wednesday’s home defeat to Bologna. With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb , the Milan owner spoke to journalist Carlo Pellegatti on Friday evening, a day before the Derby della Madonnina at San Siro, which kicks off at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT]. “It’s a fantastic night. Tomorrow is a big game,” he said. “My job isn’t to increase the emotions. My job is to keep everything steady and focused, and to provide the leadership so we do what we need to do. Tomorrow we need to win the first 45 minutes and then the next ones. “It’s a long season, but this is our home derby, I want it more than anything else, and I’ll be devastated if we don’t win.” ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, looks on before the Serie A match between AC Milan and Bologna FC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Cardinale backs Amorim after Milan defeat to Bologna Milan are fifth on 18 points, seven behind leaders Inter and Lazio. Wednesday’s 4-2 loss to Bologna was their first league defeat under Amorim. A derby defeat would leave them 10 points off the top, and the Portuguese coach’s position is already being questioned. Cardinale, who was at San Siro for the Bologna game , made it clear he has no doubts. “We need to stay united. Everyone, the fans, the press, everyone must support Milan,” he said. “Ruben is doing a great job, I made a great choice. He really cares. He’s coaching, he’s mentoring, and I’ve met every one of the players. I looked them in the eyes, and I’m telling you they want to win. “It’s just a matter of time. Either you want to win or you don’t. I want to win, the boys do, and so does Amorim.”

item.title: Prep talk: Freshman Keon'Dre Smith of Bellflower puts together terrific season
item.description: Freshman receiver Keon'Dre Smith of Bellflower High. (Eric Sondheimer / Los Angeles Times) Freshman receiver Keon’Dre Smith doesn’t need to wear a scary costume on Halloween. He just needs to show up wearing his No. 4 jersey for Bellflower High, because he really is a top football player who makes life miserable for defensive backs. Freshman Keondre Smith punt return for touchdown. 14-0 Bellflower over Gahr. pic.twitter.com/NNWbCcJGXZ — eric sondheimer (@latsondheimer) October 30, 2026 In 10 regular-season games, he finished with 83 receptions for 1,531 yards and 16 touchdowns on the varsity team. He just received a scholarship offer from UCLA. On Thursday night against Gahr, Smith had a 78-yard punt return for a touchdown and caught touchdown passes of 31 and five yards. item.title: Verstappen’s race simulations offer reason for optimism after a chaotic practice session and grid penalty
item.description: Max Verstappen finished FP2 in Mexico with damage to his car and the fifth-fastest time. His longer run gives Red Bull Racing something to build on, as he was close to George Russell . For now, it remains unclear how much faster Verstappen could be with a repaired car. His run also did not include the later phase, when several rivals began to lose pace. Verstappen made contact with Liam Lawson in FP1, and the incident affected the rest of his session. Technical director Pierre Waché confirmed that the damage had hurt performance and would be repaired in time for FP3. He felt the long run was reasonably solid, but also saw room to work on the balance. Neither driver was satisfied with it yet. Verstappen finds his pace again after a slower lap Despite that, Verstappen’s average of 1:21.490 on the soft tyre is reasonably encouraging. Russell recorded 1:21.442 on the same compound, a difference of just 0.048 seconds. Lando Norris was a little bit quicker with 1:21.319. In this sample, the Dutchman therefore averaged less than two tenths behind the fastest driver. One notable feature of Verstappen’s run is that after an opening lap of 1:21.963, he completed three laps between 1:21.170 and 1:21.260. Those laps were closely grouped. Even after a break and a slower 1:22.020, he returned to his earlier pace with a 1:21.276. His final recorded lap was a 1:21.523. There it is also important to point out that Verstappen only did seven laps. Russell and Norris did nine and eleven, respectively. Their longer runs provide a clearer picture of what their cars and tyres can do. Red Bull can be pleased that it remained in the mix despite the damage, but there is not enough evidence to conclude that Verstappen would have had the best race pace without it. The extent of the time lost is unknown, and a longer stint could expose other issues. Isack Hadjar ranks ahead of Verstappen in the comparison and is close behind Norris. That looks strong for Red Bull, but his average is based on just five laps. His final two laps were also clearly slower than those at the start of his run. The Frenchman's early pace is encouraging, but it remains uncertain whether he can sustain it over a full stint. The gap to Verstappen therefore says little about their relative performance: Hadjar completed a shorter run, while Verstappen was dealing with damage. Because both Red Bull runs were relatively short, there is no convincing picture of tyre degradation. The initial pace is there, but based on these times, the team has little reason to feel confident about how long it can be maintained. Norris gives Red Bull a strong benchmark Norris combines the best average on the softs with a longer run, making him a useful benchmark for Red Bull. His pace does drop over the course of the run, but he manages to improve again at the end, so McLaren is not showing a sustained decline either. item.title: Third weekend of protests in France
item.description: France is preparing for a third weekend of protests, with 70,000 security personnel deployed to prevent a repeat of the violence seen on October 17. Shops have boarded up their premises as authorities warn of further clashes, with Halloween adding to concerns over masked demonstrators. The protests, initially driven by anger over the cost of living and poor school conditions, have broadened to include demands for greater civil liberties and the right to protest. With presidential elections six months away, authorities have tightened security and restricted demonstrations in several cities.

item.title: Bruins Face Surprising Atlantic Division Reality After Two Straight Losses
item.description: Bruins Face Surprising Atlantic Division Reality After Two Straight Losses originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins entered the final weekend of October with a division lead, a winning record and plenty of reasons to feel encouraged about their opening month.They also entered it with two consecutive losses and a reminder that the Atlantic Division might not provide much room for mistakes. Boston hosts the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday after falling 2-1 to the Carolina Hurricanes on Tuesday and 4-1 to the St. Louis Blues on Thursday. Those defeats interrupted an eight-game point streak in which the Bruins went 7-0-1. The Bruins still own a 9-4-1 record, but their position atop the division comes with an unusual complication. Every Atlantic Division team entered Saturday with a points percentage of at least .577. That makes Boston's impressive opening month feel less comfortable than its record might suggest. A Strong Start Has Suddenly Become A Test The Bruins have already demonstrated their ability to win different types of games. They put together an extended point streak, generated late offense and found contributions beyond their biggest stars. Their six-goal comeback victory against San Jose was one of the clearest examples of that resilience. A Friday reset 💪 https://t.co/nSZ80RpdpP — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 30, 2026 But the last two games have been different. Boston scored only twice combined against Carolina and St. Louis. The Bruins were unable to produce the kind of offensive response that helped fuel their earlier success. That does not erase what they accomplished during their point streak, but it creates an important early-season question. Can Boston consistently manufacture offense when opponents prevent its top players from controlling the game? A Historic Goal Is Waiting David Pastrnak enters Saturday with 427 career goals, tied with Patrice Bergeron for third in Bruins franchise history. His next goal would move him into sole possession of third place, behind only Johnny Bucyk and Phil Esposito. The milestone would be significant for Pastrnak, particularly in his first season as Boston's captain. But the Bruins need more than a memorable individual moment. They need to restore the offensive rhythm that helped them climb to the top of the Atlantic. Chicago arrives with a 4-9-0 record and just one win in its last five games. The Blackhawks have scored only six goals during that stretch. On paper, the opponent offers Boston a favorable opportunity to respond. item.title: Dallas Stars, seeking consistency, conclude homestand vs. Columbus Blue Jackets
item.description: The Dallas Stars will try to conclude their six-game homestand on a high note when they entertain the Columbus Blue Jackets on Oct. 31. The Stars have dropped back-to-back one-sided games following a five-game winning streak. After losing 5-1 on Oc.t 27 to the New Jersey Devils , who were debuting newly acquired three-time Vezina Trophy winner Connor Hellebuyck in goal, the Stars absorbed a 5-2 loss on Oct. 29 to the Montreal Canadiens . "Our puck play is atrocious right now," Dallas coach Glen Gulutzan said after the latest loss. The Stars have already shown they can turn things around in a hurry. They lost their first two games of the season before posting back-to-back shutouts against the San Jose Sharks and Buffalo Sabres . Dallas responded to its next two-game losing streak by winning five in a row. Gulutzan knows what it will take to snap the latest skid. "You can say maybe you're lacking a little confidence, or you're a little tentative, but the only way to get it is to dig in," Gulutzan said. "You can't hand somebody confidence. You've got to put in the work, and you've got to be focused. We need to bear down." Gulutzan said the Stars will get some reinforcements on Saturday. Esa Lindell rotated in on a couple defensive pairings at practice on Friday after missing five games with a lower-body injury, and forwards Radek Faksa and David Perron are also close to joining the lineup. Faksa has missed three games with a lower-body injury, and the 38-year-old Perron has been getting up to speed after signing as a free agent two weeks ago. Gulutzan said at least one from that trio will play against the Blue Jackets, and possibly two. A forward spot opened on the roster when the Stars sent Matthew Seminoff down to AHL affiliate Texas on Friday. The Blue Jackets are coming off a 3-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday in Raleigh, N.C, which came on the heels of back-to-back overtime victories for their first two-game winning streak of the season. Columbus put itself in a 3-0 hole in the loss to the Hurricanes before scoring twice in the first 10 minutes of the third period. They managed just one shot on Carolina goalie Pyotr Kochetkov over the final seven minutes, however. "We go down three, and we see our fight and what we have, but we have to bring that early on," Columbus forward Charlie Coyle said. "No matter what happens, we have to stick on that script. We didn't start with it, and it hurt us inthe end." Columbus coach Rick Bowness echoed what Coyle said after the loss. The Blue Jackets lost the first period against the Hurricanes, but won the next two. Unfortunately, it's the scoreboard that counts. "I know we lost, but our best hockey is going to be ahead of us if we play like that for 60 minutes like we played the last two (periods)," Bowness said. item.title: Clay Travis says WNBA’s national anthem facade is to turn away Donald Trump supporters
item.description: Photo by Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images OutKick founder Clay Travis has figured out the real reason behind the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries leaving the court during the US national anthem. The 2026 WNBA Finals are just one game away from the conclusion, as the series has been pushed to Game 7 following the Atlanta Dream’s stunning win in Game 6. While fans are excited to see which team will be crowned the champions of the W, one thing that has been impossible to ignore is the Dream and Golden State Valkyries players leaving the court during the US national anthem. The players have faced several accusations for their actions, but OutKick founder Clay Travis has tied their actions to US President Donald Trump. Clay Travis believes WNBA players do not want Donald Trump supporters to become fans During a recent segment on FOX News, Travis shared his honest opinion on WNBA players leaving the hardwood during the national anthem. He believes the likes of Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham’s rise to stardom has made Trump supporters fans of the league, and the rest of the players are simply against this. “What’s really going on here is the WNBA has a far left-wing fan base that is fueled by identity politics. Lots of gay fans, lots of minority fans. “And when they brought in Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham started to get a lot of attention, they started to get the larger community that’s also interested,” Travis said. He added, “Now they’ve got Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham is connected to her and they won’t embrace either of these women. I think it’s because they’re white and they happen to be straight and they don’t like the fact that Trump’s voters, Trump supporters might suddenly like their league.” “And that’s why I really think they’re doing things like this anthem. They’re shooting themselves in the foot,” the OutKick founder concluded. Travis’ claim convinced FOX News host Lawrence Jones, as he added that the rest of the WNBA players want to ‘destroy their league.’ Jones believes that the players should enjoy their perks due to the likes of Clark and Cunningham. Now, that’s a serious accusation and one that could result in both Jones and Travis being scolded by WNBA players on social media.
